memory_update.text: Chemtrade is the cleaner sulphuric-acid/logistics underfollowed candidate in this chunk, but its survival past Layer 2 requires primary-source proof that sulphuric acid and related logistics are material to margin and not fully pass-through.

Hawkins is a weaker but plausible second-order chemical-distribution candidate; the main gating item is whether sulphuric acid or related inorganic acids are material enough to affect Industrial Solutions economics.

Sterling Infrastructure should be mapped as an AI site-enablement and mission-critical construction candidate rather than a pure electrical-equipment candidate until evidence shows direct electrical balance-of-plant exposure.

Curtiss-Wright is a hidden nuclear-qualified component candidate; primary diligence must isolate commercial nuclear, AP1000, SMR, uprate, and restart exposure from broader aerospace and defense backlog.

Compass Diversified is a hidden-subsidiary magnet thesis through Arnold; it should remain in the underfollowed lane only if Arnold is material to consolidated EBITDA/NAV and has defensible Western or defense-qualified magnet exposure.

Vertiv, BWXT, X-Energy, and Coherent are reference or context anchors in this chunk; they should not crowd out underfollowed candidates but should define evidence standards for backlog, qualification, capacity, and customer validation.

Need primary-source company filings and transcripts for CGIFF/CHE.UN, HWKN, STRL, CW, CODI, VRT, BWXT, XE, and COHR to verify segment revenue, backlog, margin sensitivity, capacity constraints, and customer exposure.

Need market-pricing checks for each candidate: market cap, analyst count, EV/EBITDA or P/E versus peers, short interest, liquidity, recent relative performance, and whether the chokepoint narrative is already reflected in valuation.

Need independent corroboration of the 2026 sulphur/sulphuric-acid disruption and its regional impact beyond the Kpler context before upgrading North American acid suppliers from hypothesis to inference or fact.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk into public-market relationships across three hotspot nodes: sulphur/sulphuric-acid feedstock and logistics, AI data-center power/site execution, and nuclear fuel/components. The strongest underfollowed relationships in this chunk are Chemtrade and Hawkins as possible North American sulphuric-acid/logistics beneficiaries, Sterling as a second-order AI infrastructure execution name, Curtiss-Wright as a hidden nuclear-qualified component supplier, and Compass Diversified as a hidden magnet-supply exposure through Arnold. Reference leaders Vertiv, BWXT, X-Energy, and Coherent are retained only as benchmarks for evidence quality and demand validation, not as the main underfollowed alpha lane. Most relationships remain inference or hypothesis because company-level revenue exposure, backlog, contract pass-through, customer mix, and margin sensitivity still require primary-source verification.
